title: Prompt to archive backlog/ after a plain --migrate-backlog migration
description:
User bug report, second half: 'when the migration is done it should also prompt to archive backlog.md from the project.' opum-agent confirmed Backlog.md has no upstream removal command to delegate to (checked its src/cli.ts registrations directly: agents board browser cleanup config decision doc draft list milestone overview sequence task view -- cleanup only moves completed tasks within a live project, it is not a teardown).

Traced the code: archiveAndDeleteBacklog/verifyArchive already exist (src/backlog-archive.ts) but are ONLY reachable via the coordinated cutover path gated on --adopt-manifest (a separate knowledge-adoption feature, src/tracker-cutover.ts) -- a plain lore init --migrate-backlog (flag or wizard) calls runBacklogMigration directly, which only migrates tasks. Zero archive step, zero prompt, backlog/ is left exactly as-is.

IMPORTANT, checked before reuse per opum-agent's explicit caution: archiveAndDeleteBacklog is more aggressive than the fleet's own 'archive means move out, never delete' convention. It genuinely DELETES the original backlog/ files after writing a verified, repository-local, GITIGNORED zip to .lore/archive/ -- not committed, not published, and NOT the external-archive-location convention CLAUDE.md describes for this fleet's own housekeeping (which doesn't apply to an arbitrary external lore user's project anyway). The deletion is done via git-uncommitted rename+unlink, so it IS recoverable via git checkout -- backlog/ until the operator commits, or by unzipping the local archive -- but this must be stated honestly in any user-facing prompt, not glossed as gentle archiving.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A plain --migrate-backlog run (flag or wizard, no --adopt-manifest) prompts whether to remove backlog/ after a successful migration, with copy that accurately describes what happens: files deleted from the working tree, a verified local zip kept at .lore/archive/ (gitignored, not committed), recoverable via git checkout -- backlog/ until committed

Decide and document whether archiveAndDeleteBacklog is reused as-is (with honest prompt copy) or a lighter variant is built, after establishing whether its --adopt-manifest-coordinated assumptions are actually separable from its core archive-and-delete mechanics
--yes/non-interactive callers get a flag to opt in or out explicitly rather than being silently prompted or silently skipped

Verified end-to-end against a real backlog+quest migration, confirming backlog/ is genuinely gone from the working tree, the zip is genuinely present and verified, and git status shows the deletion as uncommitted

implementationNotes:
CORRECTION (opum-agent, 2026-09-09), narrowing the earlier caution rather than reversing this task's own decision-not-to-assume: the fleet's own 'archive means move out, never delete' convention governs THIS FLEET's own repositories and operational artifacts (disposable working copies, an archive that outlives them) -- it does not automatically transfer to what a published CLI does inside an EXTERNAL USER's own project, where git is the archive and has been all along. Removing tracked files from a working tree git preserves is an ordinary, recoverable operation, not the irreversible one that fleet rule guards against. So archiveAndDeleteBacklog deleting originals after a verified local zip is NOT obviously wrong the way the earlier note implied.

What actually matters, narrower and now the correct framing for whoever implements this: the prompt must describe accurately what it does. If it removes backlog/ and relies on git for recovery, say exactly that -- 'remove backlog/ (recoverable from git history)' -- not 'archive'. It must NOT offer to remove anything untracked or uncommitted, since for those git is not a safety net and the operation genuinely is irreversible (a real, additional precondition to check before offering the prompt at all -- confirm backlog/ is fully committed and clean before offering removal). The gitignored, repository-local zip archiveAndDeleteBacklog also writes is not a durable artifact on its own (not committed, not published) -- the real preservation mechanism for anything already committed is git itself, and the prompt copy should say that plainly rather than imply the zip is the safety net.

This still leaves the reuse-vs-lighter-variant decision open for whoever picks this up -- now better informed rather than pre-constrained by a rule that didn't apply, not resolved in either direction.

AC#2 DECISION — reuse archiveAndDeleteBacklog AS-IS; no lighter variant.

Separability, established before deciding rather than assumed: archiveAndDeleteBacklog(root, zip, id, txn) takes a repo root, a ZipWriter, an id fragment, and an injectable fs seam. Read against src/tracker-cutover.ts, it reads no CutoverPlan, writes no .lore/cutover/state.json, and references neither --adopt-manifest, the adoption ledger, nor the Quest receipt. Everything --adopt-manifest-coordinated about the existing call site lives in the COORDINATOR: applyCutover supplies `id` from its own Quest digest, gates the call on both legs verifying, and persists phase=archived + evidence afterwards. That is caller-side ordering, not an assumption baked into the leg. The one residual coupling is cosmetic and transient: the commit-boundary staging directory is renamed under .lore/cutover/, and the transaction prunes it on success (or names it in the error when it cannot).

Why reuse rather than build lighter: the verification pipeline IS the feature. plan -> build -> verify -> re-hash every source -> atomic directory rename -> re-verify the staged tree -> unlink -> prune is what makes "every original file is either recoverably on disk or in the verified archive" true at every exit point, and the prompt copy promises exactly that. A lighter variant would be a SECOND, less-verified deletion path over the same user files, for no gain — the cost of reuse is one extra zip and inventory in a gitignored directory.

One honesty defect found and fixed while establishing this: backlog-archive.ts's header invariant claims the archive is "gitignored", and in a lore-scaffolded repository it was NOT — .lore/.gitignore (core/scaffold.ts) ignores cache/ only, so the zip was an ordinary untracked file a `git add -A` would commit. buildArchive now writes .lore/archive/.gitignore ("*", which git honours for a file it is itself ignoring), idempotently and never overwriting an operator's own. AC#1's phrase "gitignored, not committed" is therefore enforced rather than asserted; proven end-to-end with `git check-ignore -q` returning 0 on the real zip and inventory.

ADDITIONAL PRECONDITION, taken from this task's own implementation note (opum-agent, 2026-09-09): removal is never offered for anything git cannot restore. backlogRemovalReadiness(root, spawn) is read-only and requires backlog/ to be BOTH tracked (`git ls-files` non-empty) and clean (`git status --porcelain -- backlog` empty); a non-worktree, a missing git binary, or any git refusal is also "not ready", because an unanswered question has not proven recovery. The wizard does not ask when it is not ready; a scripted --remove-backlog is refused with `denied` (exit 4).

VERIFICATION EVIDENCE (versions recorded, not just exit codes): lore built from this branch via `bun run src/cli.ts` (package 0.7.0), quest 0.7.1, backlog 1.50.1, bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0, macOS darwin 27.0.0.

AC#4 end-to-end, in a scratch directory created for it and nowhere else (real `backlog init` + two real tasks, committed, real `quest init`, then `lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog --remove-backlog --json`): exit 0; migration state=applied with 2 mappings, digest 83e06320feb0076f1cd837e1782b34f39f1f893d043bfc9234354990742061f0; envelope carried backlogRemoval={"removed":true,"zipRel":".lore/archive/backlog-83e06320feb0076f1cd837e1.zip","entryCount":3}; `backlog/` GONE from the working tree; the zip and its inventory present, and `git check-ignore -q` returned 0 for both (so "gitignored, not committed" is enforced); `git status --porcelain -- backlog` showed the three deletions as uncommitted (" D backlog/config.yml" and both task files); `git checkout -- backlog` restored all three files, which is the exact recovery the prompt copy promises.

Three more real-binary runs, each in its own scratch repository: neither flag -> exit 0, backlog/ kept, stderr named both flags ("backlog/ was left in place: ..."), envelope reason "no --remove-backlog/--no-remove-backlog"; --no-remove-backlog -> exit 0, kept, NO notice; --remove-backlog over a backlog/config.yml with an uncommitted edit -> error_type "denied", exit 4, message "refusing --remove-backlog: backlog/ has uncommitted changes, which git could not restore after a deletion", backlog/ untouched.

Suite: 3190 pass / 1 skip on this branch (bun test), the single failure being test/ladybug-version-qualification.test.ts's ENOENT on node_modules/@ladybugdb/core, a pre-existing worktree environment gap unrelated to this change. tsc --noEmit clean; biome check clean of errors (3 pre-existing warnings, none in changed lines); `lore check --plain` exit 0, 80 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Mutation check (each mutant applied alone, then reverted; prediction written from the test file before running). M1 remove the wizard's readiness gate -> 1 red: "an UNRECOVERABLE backlog/ is never offered". M2 drop the scripted "left in place" notice -> 1 red: "a scripted run with NEITHER flag ... is never silent". M3 drop the clean check in backlogRemovalReadiness -> 4 red: the dirty-refusal case, the real-git case, the scripted refusal, and the never-offered case. M4 flip the removal prompt's default to yes -> 1 red: "the offered default is NO". M5 stop writing .lore/archive/.gitignore -> 2 red: the gitignore unit test and the wizard end-to-end case's check-ignore assertion. M6 drop the tracked check -> 1 red: "an UNTRACKED backlog/ is refused". Every mutant localised to the cases naming its assertion; none reddened the suite wholesale.

WHERE THIS PROMPT SITS RELATIVE TO LCLI-519: it is post-write, deliberately, and is the second named exception to the wizard's "every question is asked before the first byte" invariant (LCLI-358.1) after LCLI-466's retry offer. It does not widen that exception's reasoning, it sits on the stronger side of it: the question does not EXIST before the migration runs. Asking up front would collect a pre-authorization to delete files on the strength of a migration that has not happened and may still refuse, and the invariant's purpose — a refused run leaves the directory as it found it — is preserved, since this question is only reachable after a migration succeeded and answering "no" leaves backlog/ exactly as found.
